title: The Shang Residence: a hilltop site opposite Chong Wen school.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #432 | THE SHANG RESIDENCE, KUCHAI LAMA
excerpt: A Melaka developer's first KL project: 449 units on a long, narrow hilltop site off Jalan Kuchai Lama, with a second private entrance and an 893 sq ft unit from about RM580,000.
takeaways: 449 units on 1.9 acres, from about RM580,000 for 893 sq ft.
A second private entrance avoids the busy Jalan Kuchai Lama frontage.
School, church and peak-hour traffic, a long walk from some car parks, and plenty of supply nearby.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: The Shang Residence has 449 units on a long, narrow hilltop site of 1.9 acres. A sub-basement on the slope gives residents a second, private entrance from the back roads. The level-eight deck has a pickleball court, a pool, a double-storey party pavilion with the gym above, and a hot pot pavilion, with an extra lift at the far end for those parked there. A rooftop dining pavilion looks towards the KL skyline.

Layouts are 893, 1,076 and 1,130 sq ft, all on the same plan apart from an extra study or bedroom in the larger ones. Sean viewed the 893 sq ft three-bedroom, from about RM580,000 at RM650 to RM700 psf. Its yard is enclosed and tiled like the interior, there is room for a breakfast island, and the wall between two bedrooms can be removed.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The site is just off Old Klang Road on Jalan Kuchai Lama, near Mid Valley and opposite SJKC Chong Wen, with two food courts, a wet market and many shops within walking distance. The developer has committed to a covered walkway to the future Old Klang Road MRT station and to realigning the junction. A church is next door.

standout.title: A yard that is already indoors
standout.body: Instead of a door to an open yard, the yard joins the kitchen with the same floor tiles, gentle ramps between, and a window already fitted to the void. Sean says owners usually spend RM5,000 to RM8,000 on that conversion, so the yard is usable from day one.

pros: Location and connectivity: Jalan Kuchai Lama and Old Klang Road lead to the Federal Highway, Mid Valley, KLCC, the NPE and Puchong, and on foot there are shops, food courts, Chong Wen, the wet market and a covered walk to the MRT, with privacy on the hilltop.

A design that makes the most of a narrow site: the secondary entrance, facilities on the hill, wide ramp roads, a double-storey clubhouse, and a layout with a merged yard and kitchen island that feels bigger than 893 sq ft.

A first project out to make a statement: the developer is established in Melaka, and from the start it specifies brands for kitchen cabinets, aircon and smart locks, with an oriental theme in marble and jade tones.
cons: Access: turning in and out of Jalan Kuchai Lama at peak hours, plus school and Sunday church traffic. The second entrance is costly but worth it.

No speed ramps, so residents parked at the far end face many ramps and a long walk to the lifts. Pick your unit with care. Sean also weighs whether the tower or the facilities should face the busy road.
Heavy supply in the area, with more empty plots to come, so check rents and median prices carefully, though auctioned units here sell quickly and rents are solid.

closing: Sean sees it as both an investment and a home, and especially suited to a young family planning to walk their child to Chong Wen.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this March 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the show unit, built in an existing office building, before the official opening, and he walked the undeveloped site.
